fact_label: Exchange control regime for foreign nationals and immigrants (SARB primary text)
value_raw: Foreign nationals temporarily resident in South Africa may, once foreign assets are declared on arrival: bank on a resident basis, freely invest/dispose of foreign assets, hold Non-resident Rand or foreign-currency accounts, and transfer accumulated South African funds abroad if the source is substantiated and the amount is reasonable relative to South African income-generating activity. Immigrants (permanent residents) get a parallel track: free disposal of foreign assets from arrival, and within 5 years of immigrating, the right to retransfer/re-export all introduced assets including growth. Resident South Africans have a R1 million/calendar-year single discretionary allowance plus a separate R10 million/calendar-year foreign capital allowance
date: 2026-01-07 (document version 1.69, circular 1-2026; directly fetched and read 2026-07-20)
notes: Closes the "direct SARB page fetch" gap flagged since 2026-07-18 ( close-out, bonus find beyond the row's own DHA scope). The document's own version-control table shows 69 revisions since 2016, most recent 2026-01-07 — a pattern of continuous incremental liberalization, not tightening or freezing. This specific guideline does NOT cover property-purchase exchange-control mechanics (e.g. the widely-reported "foreigner may finance up to 50% of a SA property purchase via local mortgage" rule) — that appears to live in a separate SARB Authorised Dealer Manual/circular, not yet directly fetched; real, narrower remaining gap, though a financing-detail question this project's own conventions treat as lower research priority than cash-purchase mechanics generally (see our records' mortgage/financing-detail note). divergence_flag left at Not yet checked: no first-hand account of a foreign national actually executing one of these transfers was found — the mechanism is primary-sourced, lived practice is not yet confirmed

fact_label: Cape Floristic Region — UNESCO World Heritage status
value_raw: Over 9,000 vascular plant species, 69% endemic, in a region occupying under 0.5% of Africa's landmass yet holding ~20% of the continent's plant life; the smallest of the world's six recognized floral kingdoms. notes: Directly relevant to the redefined "Income viability" criterion (per our records: not scoped to remote/passive income only — ceramics, a café, in-person tutoring are live possibilities too) — this is the actual compliance mechanism anyone earning non-salary income inside South Africa's tax-residency net would face, not previously captured as a fact row. Only applies once SA tax residency is triggered (see the 183-day rule elsewhere in this file) — a foreign remote worker on a Remote Work Visa taxed only abroad under a Double Taxation Agreement would not be a South African provisional taxpayer at all; this row describes the mechanism for whoever does cross that line, not a universal requirement. fact_label: Remote Work Visa (Digital Nomad Visa) -- max duration
notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-24 ([specialist], fixing [specialist] Return for revision of our records, fact-gap our records). The prior value (12 months) rested on a quoted sentence -- "Duration: up to 12 months initially, renewable annually for a total of up to 3 years" -- that a direct read of the the Department of Home Affairs (DHA) PDF's actual raw text (both pages, confirmed by opening the saved document itself and reading its raw text directly rather than relying on any summary of it) shows is NOT present anywhere in the document. The PDF's only duration language is its own title: "VISITORS VISA SECTION 11(1)(B)(iv) FOR PRESCRIBED ACTIVITY OF REMOTE WORK (EXCEEDING 3 MONTHS TO 3 YEARS)" -- a checklist/tax-compliance-notes document with no stated 12-month-initial/annual-renewal mechanism at all. Re-derived from the actual governing law: South Africa's Immigration Act, 2002 (Act No. 13 of 2002), Government Gazette Vol. 443 No. 23478, 31 May 2002 -- read directly, full text -- Section 11(1) Visitor's Permit: "(i) cannot exceed three months and upon application may be renewed... or (ii) may be issued... upon application for any period not to exceed three years to a foreigner who has satisfied the Department that he or she controls sufficient available financial resources... and is engaged in the Republic in (aa) academic sabbaticals; (bb) voluntary or charitable activities; (cc) research; or (dd) other prescribed activities and cases." Remote work is one of these 'other prescribed activities' (hence the later regulatory subsection numbering 11(1)(b)(iv)) and inherits this same statutory shape: DHA issues a SINGLE grant, for a period determined by the Department (not a fixed 12-month term), with a ceiling of 3 years -- exactly matching the PDF's own title framing ("exceeding 3 months to 3 years"), not a 12-month-initial-then-annual-renewal structure. value_raw corrected to 36 months (the statutory ceiling for a single grant under this mechanism) -- this is the maximum achievable single-grant duration, not a guaranteed default; actual grants may run anywhere from just over 3 months up to 36 months at DHA's discretion, likely tied to the length of the underlying foreign employment contract (no primary source found stating the allocation criteria in more detail). Confidence held at Medium: the 3-year ceiling is now primary-institutional-sourced (the Act itself, directly read, cross-matching the DHA PDF's own title), but the exact within-band allocation mechanism is not spelled out anywhere found this session.

The prior value ("renewable-limited: renewable annually for a total of up to 3 years") was the same fabricated the Department of Home Affairs (DHA)-PDF quote as the companion max_duration row -- see that row's notes for the full direct-Read disproof. Section 11(1)(b) of the Immigration Act, 2002 (directly read, Government Gazette Vol. 443 No. 23478) states this permit category "may be issued... upon application for any period not to exceed three years" -- a single-grant ceiling, not an annual-renewal cycle -- and does not itself address whether or how the permit can be renewed once that single grant expires (unlike Section 11(1)(a)'s ordinary 3-month visitor permit, which explicitly says "may be renewed by the Department"). One real, live, independently-reachable secondary source (xpatweb.com, a practicing South African immigration law firm) does describe a genuine renewal step -- "Apply for a renewal prior to the expiry of your visa while maintaining your employment and ensuring you meet the income requirements" -- confirming SOME renewal process exists in practice, but it does not state how many times, whether it resets or extends the 3-year ceiling, or any other mechanic. No primary DHA/regulatory source found this session addresses this gap. Held as a genuine open question, not restated as the fabricated 'annual renewal to 3 years total' structure -- a reader relying on this route past a single up-to-3-year grant should not assume indefinite or automatic continuation.
